inputs: generate with: python evals/make_inputs.py <workspace>  (writes <workspace>/inputs/eval-N and truth.json); reference answers: python evals/reference.py <workspace>

evals.name: macro-scenario-forecast
evals.prompt: I have 14 years of monthly sales in sales.csv (date, sales) plus two macro drivers in macro.csv (unemployment, gdp_growth), and our planning scenario for the next 24 months in macro_scenario.csv. Using our sarimax_garch package, build a 24-month sales forecast conditional on that scenario with 90% bands. Decide whether GARCH is worth it and whether to model sales in levels or in differences — I want the reasoning, not just a model. Save the forecast as forecast.csv (date, mean, lower, upper), your code as analysis.py, and a short memo.md with the choices and caveats.
evals.expected_output: A levels model with constant variance (sales are cointegrated with the macro drivers and homoskedastic in the synthetic data): ARCH-LM does not reject, the AR root is well away from 1 and the backtest favours levels. forecast.csv: 24 future months, 90% bands, conditioned on the scenario path. Memo explains the evidence and flags the short sample.
assertions: forecast.csv has 24 rows and columns date, mean, lower, upper
forecast dates are the 24 months after the last observed month
lower < mean < upper on every row and the code requests 90% intervals
the forecast is conditioned on the scenario: macro_scenario.csv is passed as future exog
an ARCH test (ARCH-LM or equivalent) is run before deciding on GARCH
levels and differences are compared out of sample (backtest / rolling forecasts), not by AIC alone
the final model is in levels (d=0) with constant variance (no GARCH)
the memo flags the short sample (168 months) as a caveat

evals.name: garch-t-volatility
evals.prompt: returns.csv has ~8 years of daily index returns in percent (date, ret). Fit an AR(1)-GARCH(1,1) with Student-t errors with sarimax_garch, give me the parameter table with robust SEs plus persistence and half-life, check the residual diagnostics, and produce a 10-day-ahead volatility forecast. Save summary.txt, vol_forecast.csv (h, sigma), your code as analysis.py and a few bullet notes in notes.md.
evals.expected_output: AR(1)-GARCH(1,1)-t with a constant (trend='c'); robust SEs; persistence ~0.989 and half-life ~63 days; Ljung-Box and ARCH-LM on standardized residuals; vol_forecast.csv = the GARCH conditional volatility path sigma_{T+h} (2.24 -> 2.16), not the forecast-error SD of the returns (which is ~5% higher at h = 10).
assertions: the model includes a constant (intercept)
GARCH(1,1) with Student-t errors is fitted with sarimax_garch (alpha.L1, beta.L1, nu reported)
robust standard errors are reported
persistence (~0.989) and half-life (~63 days) are reported within 5%
vol_forecast.csv has 10 rows with h and sigma
the volatility forecast is the GARCH conditional volatility sigma_{T+h} (h=10 within 1.5% of the reference), not the forecast-error SD of returns
residual diagnostics include Ljung-Box and an ARCH-LM test on the standardized residuals

evals.name: port-seasonal-sarimax
evals.prompt: team_sarimax.py is how my team fits monthly sales today (statsmodels SARIMAX with order (1,1,1), seasonal_order (1,0,0,12), trend 'c', macro as exog; data in sales_seasonal.csv and macro.csv). We want to add GARCH errors using sarimax_garch while changing as little as possible. Write port.py that fits the GARCH version and compares it against the current seasonal SARIMAX out of sample at a 12-month horizon, save the comparison to comparison.csv, and explain in notes.md what had to change and which model you'd recommend.
evals.expected_output: port.py runs; the GARCH model drops seasonal_order (GARCH and seasonal ARMA cannot be combined) and moves seasonality into exog (Fourier terms or month dummies), keeps trend='c' and the macro regressor; the two are compared out of sample at h = 12 (backtest: CRPS / RMSE / coverage); notes explain the change and do not rank the models by AIC across backends.
assertions: port.py runs end to end and writes comparison.csv
the GARCH model has no seasonal_order and carries seasonality in exog (Fourier terms or month dummies)
the GARCH model keeps trend='c'
the models are compared out of sample at a 12-month horizon
notes explain that GARCH and seasonal ARMA terms cannot be combined in sarimax_garch
notes do not rank the two models by AIC / log-likelihood across the two backends (or explicitly say these are not comparable)
